properties.name: management.endpoint.security-encryption.access
properties.description: Permitted level of access for the securityEncryption endpoint.

properties.name: management.endpoint.security-encryption.cache.time-to-live
properties.description: Maximum time that a response can be cached.

properties.name: security.crypto.default-key-id
properties.description: Which key id is used when a call site doesn't specify one.

properties.name: security.crypto.encrypted-api.enabled
properties.description: Master switch for @EncryptedAPI specifically. Defaults to true.

properties.name: security.crypto.encrypted-api.header-name
properties.description: The header a caller sets to indicate ITS request body is encrypted and needs decryption. Checked case-sensitively by name, compared case-insensitively by value against headerTrueValue.

properties.name: security.crypto.encrypted-api.header-true-value
properties.description: The header value that means "yes, this request body is encrypted".

properties.name: security.crypto.encrypted-api.payload-field-name
properties.description: The JSON field name both directions use to carry the ciphertext - a client sends {"<payloadFieldName>": "<ciphertext>"} for a decrypt-requesting request, and receives the same shape back for an @EncryptedAPI response.

properties.name: security.crypto.key-env-prefix
properties.description: Environment variable prefix EnvKeyProvider falls back to when a key id isn't in the `keys` map.

properties.name: security.crypto.keys
properties.description: Base64-encoded key material, keyed by key id - the simplest source for EnvKeyProvider. In any environment handling real data, prefer supplying your own KeyProvider bean backed by KMS/Vault instead of populating this map with production key material in plain application.yml.

properties.name: management.endpoint.security-encryption.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable the securityEncryption endpoint.
